title: Ines and the Ghost
premise: Juniper Voss, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a calendar invite from his handler, Ines, who died six months ago. Following the invitation's trail, he uncovers a plot within his own agency: an attack staged to look like an industrial accident, timed to destroy evidence of Meridian's darkest operation before a dawn extraction flight erases everyone involved. Hunted by colleagues he once trusted and guided by a dead woman's prearranged breadcrumbs, Juniper must decide whether loyalty to the institution that made him matters more than the truth it will kill to protect. He stops the attack at dawn but chooses exile over silence, walking away with the proof—and with the knowledge that 'Ines' was never one person, but a role he has now inherited.
about_author: Jude Reyes is the pen name of a former logistics contractor who spent a decade writing operational briefings before turning to fiction. They live somewhere unremarkable, keep a go-bag out of habit, and answer questions about their past with a polished smile.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Six months after handler Ines Kovač's funeral, Juniper receives a calendar invite from her account for tomorrow, 04:00. His instinct says trap; his grief says go. Emotional beat: the polished lie of his controlled life cracks for the first time.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. He runs counter-surveillance through the city, checking dead drops and finding them all already serviced—someone is ahead of him. A burner message in Ines's cipher: 'You were always the backup.' Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Meridian House
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. At the embassy-that-doesn't-exist, Deputy Director Callum Reeve reassures him about 'residual account activity' while quietly reactivating Juniper's clearance. Juniper notices the extraction flight manifest lists names of people already dead. Beat: institutional unease.

chapters.title: Ines's Apartment
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. He breaks into her sealed flat and finds it untouched except for a fresh cup of coffee and a locked case keyed to his biometrics. Inside: partial schematics for the Halvard freight terminal. Beat: intimacy with the dead, and the first hard evidence.

chapters.title: The Accident File
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. The schematics match a scheduled 'maintenance incident'—a gas release timed for 05:30 tomorrow that will kill forty contractors and bury records of Operation LANTERN. Beat: cold horror as coincidence becomes design.

chapters.title: Old Colleagues
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. He approaches former teammate Mara Ilic, now security chief at Halvard. She warns him off, then slips him a keycard—she received an invite too. Beat: fragile alliance; loyalty tested against fear.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV flashbacks interwoven with present. We learn Ines trained Juniper, and that 'Ines' was a rotating cover identity used by three officers over twenty years. Beat: identity destabilizes—who exactly died, and who is inviting him?

chapters.title: Reeve's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Reeve offers him a seat on the dawn flight, promotion, and a clean slate—if he stops asking about LANTERN. The offer itself confirms the conspiracy. Beat: temptation and contempt in equal measure.

chapters.title: Mara's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Mara. She audits the terminal's safety systems and finds the gas-line 'upgrade' signed off by a dead engineer. Her loyalty to Meridian wavers as she realizes she was placed at Halvard to be the accident's credible witness. Beat: betrayal.

chapters.title: The Second Invite
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Another message from Ines's account directs him to a train station locker containing her real diary—and a photo of three women who all served as 'Ines,' one of them alive. Beat: hope rekindled, paranoia doubled.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Meridian's internal hunters pick up his trail; a rooftop chase ends with him barely escaping, wounded. He realizes Reeve let him run—he's being used to find any other conspirators. Beat: exhaustion, hunted-animal clarity.

chapters.title: LANTERN
chapters.summary: POV Juniper reading the diary. Operation LANTERN sold identities of protected informants, causing deaths abroad; the 'accident' destroys its paper trail. Ines had been building a case when she died—or was killed. Beat: moral reckoning with what he served.

chapters.title: The Living Ines
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. He contacts Elena Brandt, the third Ines, retired and hiding in a coastal town. She confirms the diary but insists she sent no invitations. Someone else is wearing the ghost. Beat: the mystery pivots—the sender is close.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Confronted by Reeve's men, she feeds them a false location for Juniper, burning her career. She transmits the terminal's override codes to him. Beat: loyalty finally aligned with truth, at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Meridian declares him compromised; airports, banks, and safehouses close to him simultaneously. With hours left, he plans entry to Halvard through the maintenance tunnels using Ines's schematics. Beat: isolation forged into resolve.

chapters.title: The Sender
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Tracing the invite metadata, he finds the sender: Tomas Reiner, Ines's protégé, who faked her death to force someone to finish her case. He's been orchestrating Juniper all along. Beat: fury and grudging respect.

chapters.title: Tunnels
chapters.summary: POV Juniper and Tomas infiltrate Halvard's underbelly, disabling alarms while above them night-shift workers unknowingly crowd the kill zone. A patrol forces them into a flooded section. Beat: claustrophobic tension, partnership under pressure.

chapters.title: What Reeve Knows
chapters.summary: POV Reeve. He isn't the architect—his superiors ordered LANTERN's erasure, and his own name is on the flight manifest as expendable. He makes a quiet call that delays the detonation sequence by ninety seconds. Beat: the villain revealed as another cog.

chapters.title: Terminal
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Climax begins: they reach the control room as the gas system arms. Mara remotely unlocks doors; Juniper physically severs the release line while Tomas holds off Meridian's cleaners. Beat: desperate, kinetic sacrifice of certainty.

chapters.title: Dawn Flight
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. The attack fails and looks like nothing at all—exactly as designed. The extraction flight leaves without him, carrying Reeve into oblivion. Juniper chooses to stay, broadcasting LANTERN's file to journalists. Beat: triumph that costs everything.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Aftermath: inquiries begin, Mara testifies, Tomas disappears. Juniper burns his own legend and builds a new one. In a final letter, he understands the invitation was Ines's last contingency—and that he is now the ghost others may someday summon. Beat: identity remade.

chapters.title: The Next Invitation
chapters.summary: POV new fixer, years later. A young officer at a nameless embassy receives a meeting invite from an account belonging to Juniper Voss—dead two years. She packs a bag. Beat: cyclical chill; the role endures, the truth keeps needing hands.
